ciphertext_source: HCPortal record 513 (api.hcportal.eu/api/cryptograms/513), image hstam_9_a_nr_259__0249.jpg, HStAM 9 a Nr. 259 f.249; own blind transcription from the image 26 Sept 2026 (ciphers/hessen-1824/images/, crops in NOTES.md), grade M throughout -- one page, Latin-letter cursive (not German Kurrent), word/group boundaries (space vs '.') uncertain, transcribed here as a continuous letter stream (dots and spaces both dropped by family_run.py's tokens=letters mode) for the periodic-IC test; a few glyphs (three occurrences of a digit-like '4' embedded in or beside words) are anomalous and excluded from the letter count below.
alphabet: a-z Latin cursive, 26-letter alphabet expected under HCPortal's own 'Polyalphabetic / Substitution' category tag

constraints.sender: Unknown (HCPortal structured field); Bourdeau CATALOGUE.md #340: 'Electorate of Hesse' chancery, unknown -> unknown
constraints.era_note: Target is dated 20 Feb 1824. tools/data/de20 (LANG_CORPORA default judge corpus used here) is 1880-1940 German prose, 56-116 years later than the target; tools/data/de16 (composed_enhg.txt) is Early New High German, further off in the other direction. No 1820s-matched German corpus is on disk (CLAUDE.md's pt18/es17c precedent for era-matching a judge corpus has not been done for this decade of German). Any PASS/FAIL from this spec's judge block should be read with that gap flagged, per the de16/de20 mismatch already logged for berthier-napoleon-1812 and other early-19th-century German targets in this project.
constraints.anmerkung_note: The same manuscript page (below the 6-line ciphertext, same image) carries a period or 19th-century archival note headed 'Anmerkung' describing a related item ('No. 1', invisible/sympathetic ink between lines) and a substitution table the annotator worked out: bcdefg(h) in the top row of a key/tableau are said to be 'Auflösungsbuchstaben' (resolution letters) placed continuously over the cipher, giving column positions of a periodic key; the worked example maps pairs of cipher letters to plaintext letters per column (approximate, uncertain reading of German Kurrent: u/c->s, f/o->c, m/e->h, o/f->i, g/g->k, ?/b->n, v->t). This was NOT applied to the ciphertext this pass (paleographic risk of misreading Kurrent under a $2 cap outweighs the value of a guessed key -- see NOTES.md); it is a strong lead for a follow-up transcription pass and is consistent with HCPortal's own 'Polyalphabetic/Substitution' category tag and with a period around 6-7.
